info.title: NCA-V4-API
info.description:
Search the news NewsCatcher has crawled in the last **30 days**, in every language: ranked by relevance, source authority and freshness, and
grouped into **stories** (the articles that report the same event), with a one-line summary of each article.

## Authentication

Send your API key in the `x-api-key` header of every request. Keys are created in the NewsCatcher platform. A missing or invalid key is answered with `401`.

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | What it does | Charged |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` or `POST /search` | Ranked articles for a request in plain words or with keywords. | Yes, by effort |
| `GET /stories/{story_id}` | Every article of one story. | Yes, 1 NCC per successful request |
| `GET /subscription` | Your plan, limits and credit balance. | No |

## Effort and credits

`effort` sets how much work goes into the ranking. A search is charged in **NCC** credits, by the effort you ask for, and only when it succeeds (`200`).

| Effort | What it does | Credits |
|---|---|---|
| `low` | Ranks by relevance, authority, coverage and freshness. Fastest. | 1 |
| `medium` (default) | Adds a cross-encoder rerank of the top stories. | 5 |
| `high` | Adds an LLM judgement of the top stories and merges the stories that report the same event. Slowest, best quality. | 10 |

A search that finds nothing is still charged. A request that is refused or fails (`401`, `402`, `403`, `422`, `429`, `500`, `503`) is never charged.

## Query

`q` is a request in plain words or keywords, in any language, up to 500 characters. Put an upper-case `NOT` before a term to drop the articles that mention it in
their headline, description or summary (`Apple NOT iPhone`). `languages`, `countries` and `sources` narrow the search; the time window is the last 24 hours unless you set
`window_hours`.

## Limits

Your plan sets the requests per second (per effort level and in all), an optional daily limit, the most results per request (`limit`) and how far back you can search.
`GET /subscription` returns all of them. Over a limit you get `429` with a `Retry-After` header. A `window_hours` longer than your plan's history is cut to it and the response
says `window.clamped`.

## Errors

Every error has the same body: `message` (what went wrong), `status_code` and `status` (a short label). Use the HTTP status to decide what to do:

| Status | Meaning | Retry the same request? |
|---|---|---|
| `401` | The API key is missing or invalid. | No |
| `402` | Your credit balance does not cover the search. | After topping up |
| `403` | The plan does not include what you asked for (a larger `limit`, an Enterprise field) or the key may not use this API. | No |
| `404` | Unknown story. | No |
| `422` | A parameter is missing, invalid or unknown, or the body is not valid JSON. | No, fix it first |
| `429` | A rate limit of your plan. | Yes, after `Retry-After` seconds |
| `500` | Something failed on our side. | Yes, and tell us the `Correlation-ID` |
| `503` | A part of the service is temporarily unavailable. | Yes, after a short wait |

Every response carries a `Correlation-ID` header (quote it to support) and an `X-Process-Time` header.

## Enterprise fields

`include` adds heavy fields to every result (`description`, `entities`, `sentiment`, `themes`, `translation`, `embedding`). They are part of the Enterprise plans;
other plans get `403` with `enterprise_field`.

get.description:
Ranked real-news articles for a request in plain words or with keywords, grouped into stories.

**How it ranks.** Every article is scored on relevance to the request, the authority of its publisher, how many newsrooms cover its story and how fresh it is.
`effort` decides how much further work goes into the order: `low` stops there, `medium` adds a cross-encoder rerank of the top stories, `high` adds an LLM judgement of
them and merges stories that report the same event. Articles in every language are searched through their English translation, unless every language you ask for is not English
(then the original language is searched).

**Filters.** `languages`, `countries`, `sources` and `min_newsrooms` narrow the search, `not_languages`, `not_countries` and `not_sources` leave articles out; `window_hours` sets the look-back window on the publication date (on the crawl date with `sort_by=crawled_at`) (24 hours by default, up to your plan's
history). `collapse` decides what happens to several articles of one story. `sort_by` is `relevancy` (default), `published_at` or `crawled_at` (newest first; it covers the best matches of `q`, not every article of the window). An upper-case `NOT` in `q` drops the articles that mention the term in their headline, description or summary.

**Credits.** A successful search (`200`) costs 1, 5 or 10 NCC for `low`, `medium` or `high` effort, also when it finds nothing. A refused or failed request is not charged.
Your balance and limits are in `GET /subscription`.

**Two ways to call it.** `GET /search` with the parameters in the query string, or `POST /search` with the same parameters as a JSON body. In both, `sources`, `languages`, `countries`, their `not_` versions
and `include` take a comma-separated string; in the JSON body they can also be arrays.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What to look for: keywords with AND/OR/NOT or a plain-language question, in any language. An upper-case `NOT` (`Apple NOT iPhone`, `NOT "model y"`) drops the articles whose headline, description or summary mention the term.

parameters.name: effort
parameters.description: How much work goes into the ranking, and the price: `low` ranks by relevance, authority, coverage and freshness (1 NCC); `medium` adds a cross-encoder rerank of the top stories (5 NCC); `high` adds an LLM rerank and merges stories about the same event (10 NCC). Charged only when the search succeeds.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of articles to return (1 to 100; a plan may allow fewer, e.g. 50 on Free: the request is refused with 403 above it).

parameters.name: collapse
parameters.description: `diverse` (default) discounts repeated articles of one story, `story` keeps one article per story, `duplicates` keeps every article (copies of one article are always one result).

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: The order of the results: `relevancy` (default) best match first; `published_at` newest publication first; `crawled_at` newest crawl first. A date order covers the best matches of `q` (at least 100, or 5 times `limit`), not every article of the window, and `collapse=diverse` then keeps every article, as `duplicates` does. A publication date later than the crawl date counts as the crawl date.

parameters.name: window_hours
parameters.description: Look-back window in hours, from 1 up to your plan's history (30 days = 720 hours on the free plan; a longer request is cut to it and the response says `window.clamped`). Default: 24.

parameters.name: sources
parameters.description: Only search these publishers: domains, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). Matches any copy of an article. The result then shows the requested domain: its name, and a link of that domain (with several matching domains on one article, the first of them in the article's order).

parameters.name: languages

items.description: ISO 639-1 language code; Chinese is `cn` (simplified) or `tw` (traditional), `zh` means `cn`.

parameters.description: Only articles in these languages: ISO 639-1 codes, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). `zh` is searched as `cn`.

parameters.name: countries
parameters.description: Only articles from publishers in these countries: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100).

parameters.name: not_sources
parameters.description: Leave out these publishers: domains, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). An article is dropped when any of its copies comes from one of them.

parameters.name: not_languages

items.description: ISO 639-1 language code; Chinese is `cn` (simplified) or `tw` (traditional), `zh` means `cn`.

parameters.description: Leave out articles in these languages: ISO 639-1 codes, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100). `zh` is excluded as `cn`.

parameters.name: not_countries
parameters.description: Leave out articles from publishers in these countries: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, comma-separated or as an array (at most 100).

parameters.name: min_newsrooms
parameters.description: Only stories carried by at least this many newsrooms.

parameters.name: content_type
parameters.description: `news` (default) keeps real news articles only; `all` returns every article, whatever its type.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Heavy fields to add to every result, comma-separated or as an array: description, entities, sentiment, themes, translation, embedding. Enterprise accounts only (403 `enterprise_field` otherwise).

200.description: The articles, best first. `count` is 0 and `results` empty when nothing matched.

NewsSearchRequest.title: NewsSearchRequest
NewsSearchRequest.description: What to search for and how. The same parameters are accepted in the query string of `GET /search` and in the JSON body of `POST /search`.

query.description: The query as received (control characters replaced, ends trimmed).

effort.description: The effort level that ran: `low`, `medium` or `high`.

sort_by.description: The order of the results: `relevancy` (best match first), `published_at` or `crawled_at` (newest first).

took_ms.description: Time the search took on our side, in milliseconds.

window.description: The time window that was searched: `hours` back from `to`, which is when the search ran.

results.description: The articles, in the order of `sort_by`.

excluded.description: The terms of the `NOT` clauses of `q`: articles whose headline, description or summary mention one are left out. Absent when `q` has no `NOT`.

NewsSearchResponse.title: NewsSearchResponse
NewsSearchResponse.description: The articles that match a search, with the window that was searched.

NewsSentiment.description: Sentiment of the article (`include=sentiment`; Enterprise): from -1 (very negative) through 0 (neutral) to 1 (very positive).

id.description: Story id; pass it to `GET /stories/{story_id}` to list every article of the story.

newsrooms.description: Number of newsrooms (distinct publishers) that cover the story.

NewsStory.title: NewsStory
NewsStory.description: The story (a group of articles about the same event) a result belongs to.

examples: Major disaster declared in Florida following Hurricane Isaias; federal aid approved

language.description: Language of the article, an ISO 639-1 code.

published_at.description: When the article was published (UTC, ISO 8601).

content_type.description: Type of content the article was classified as.

NewsStoryArticle.title: NewsStoryArticle
NewsStoryArticle.description: One distinct article of a story.

articles_total.description: Number of distinct articles of the story.

newsrooms.description: Number of newsrooms (distinct publishers) that cover the story.

first_seen.description: Publication time of the earliest article (UTC, ISO 8601).

last_seen.description: Publication time of the latest article (UTC, ISO 8601).

articles.description: The articles of the story, best sources first.

articles.title: Major disaster declared in Florida following Hurricane Isaias; federal aid approved

examples: He searched for the right word and found it.
Maja Chwalińska won the WTA 1000 tournament in Wuhan and reached the final of Roland Garros.

NewsTranslation.title: NewsTranslation
NewsTranslation.description: English translation of a non-English article (`include=translation`; Enterprise). Parts that do not exist are left out.

hours.description: Length of the window in hours, counted back from `to`.

to.description: End of the window: the moment the search ran (UTC, ISO 8601).

clamped.description: True when the requested window was longer than your plan allows and was cut to it. Absent otherwise.

NewsWindow.title: NewsWindow
NewsWindow.description: The time window that was searched.

max_articles_per_page.description: Largest `limit` your plan allows; a larger one is refused with 403.

historical_days.description: How many days back your plan allows searching; a longer `window_hours` is cut to it.

requests_per_second.description: Requests per second allowed for your whole organization, per effort level.

shared_requests_per_second.description: Requests per second allowed for your organization across all effort levels, if limited.

daily_request_limit.description: Requests allowed per UTC day, if limited. Null when your plan has no daily limit.

credits_per_search.description: NCC one successful search costs, per effort level.

story.description: Story pages: whether your plan allows them, their requests per second and their price.

extra_fields.description: Heavy article fields your plan unlocks with `include`. Empty when your plan has none.

credits_balance.description: Remaining NCC credits. Cached for up to 2 minutes, and usage reaches it 1 to 3 minutes late.

OrganizationSubscriptionResponse.title: OrganizationSubscriptionResponse
OrganizationSubscriptionResponse.description: Plan, limits and credits of the authenticated organization.

enabled.description: Whether your plan allows story pages; when it does not they are refused with 403.

requests_per_second.description: Story requests per second allowed for your whole organization. 0 when story pages are not enabled.

credits_per_request.description: NCC a successful story request costs, whatever the number of articles returned.

ApiKeyAuth.description: Your NewsCatcher API key, created in the NewsCatcher platform. Send it in the `x-api-key` header of every request.
ApiKeyAuth.name: x-api-key

Correlation-ID.description: Id of this request. Quote it when you contact support: it finds the request in our logs.

X-Process-Time.description: Seconds the API spent on the request.
